To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the physician’s capacity to see patients is the most important factor in determining the performance of a primary health care clinic.
the physician’s examining room capacity and the patient flow rate are the two most significant variables affecting patient flow and resource use at the clinic.
increased resource utilization does increase the length of the waiting line and patient flow time, but not necessarily in the same proportion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the impact of examining room capacity on clinic performance.
the development of an analytical model for the study of outpatient clinics.
the application of simulation modeling techniques to the analysis of health care delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physician’s clinic is a complex system and that the results of a discrete-event simulation model of the clinic are useful for understanding and improving its performance.
a physician should not expect a decrease in patient flow time when he/she increases the number of examination rooms.
increased capacity in the examining room is not necessarily associated with decreased waiting times.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this research provide a foundation for the development of a simulation-based decision support system to assist physicians with the design and operation of their own practices.
the simulation model is a valuable tool in the analysis of outpatient clinic operations, especially when considering the tradeoffs between performance and cost.
the results of this study provide a framework for future studies in this area, and that the simulation model developed here can be used as a tool in the evaluation of outpatient clinic operations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between resource utilization and performance is not necessarily linear.
the relationship between resource utilization and patient flow is complex, non-linear, and dependent on many factors.
it is possible to improve the performance of a clinic without increasing resource utilization.
